title: Conversations with an AI chatbot durably reduce conspiracy beliefs
summary: Across experiments with more than 2,000 participants, three dialogues with GPT-4 reduced belief in the targeted conspiracy theory by about 20%, and the effect persisted for two months and spilled over to unrelated conspiracies. A professional fact-checker rated 99.2% of 128 sampled chatbot claims as true. Caveats: lab setting, the chatbot did not reduce belief in true conspiracies, and most participants still held the hoax belief.
organization: MIT Sloan School of Management; Cornell University; American University

evidence.tested: More than 2,000 conspiracy believers held three personalized, evidence-based dialogues with GPT-4 Turbo, and belief change was measured, including persistence at two months and spillover to unrelated conspiracies.
evidence.unknown: The abstract does not describe a control group and states no limitations; the page metadata lists a 2026 expression of concern and erratum.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-4 Turbo delivered the personalized counterevidence in the dialogues.
